svg.text: BEST FOR: CALIBRATED BINARY RUBRIC JUDGES
FORMAT LINEAGE: Hamel Husain • Shreya Shankar • Eugene Yan • Vertex AI Eval & Promptfoo
Before You Trust an LLM-as-a-Judge Dashboard: Calibrate TPR, TNR & Cohen's κ Like a Lab Instrument
Deterministic hard-gates run first (0 tokens); calibrated binary rubric judges run second across different model families (Gemini 3.8 / Claude / Open-Weights).
100 hand-labeled production traces; require TPR >= 0.90 and TNR >= 0.90 before gating CI/CD.
5 KNOWN JUDGE BIASES → THE FIX THAT ACTUALLY WORKS
A model family rates its own
mode with a quoted trace span.
JUDGE PROMPT SKELETON (COPY, THEN FILL THE RUBRIC)
SYSTEM: Grade ONE binary failure mode only.
PASS = every claimed action matches a tool receipt
FAIL = any claimed action lacks a verified receipt
DO NOT reward length, tone, or formatting.
# Release gate: compare against 50 human labels;
Every release: run deterministic hard-gates (schema, exit_code,
SHA receipt) first; then re-grade 50 human-labeled traces with a
cross-family binary judge; block deploy if TNR drops >5 pts.
Watch TNR (does the judge catch real failures?) — a lenient judge with 95% TPR and 60% TNR quietly hides production regressions.
Deterministic First: Never pay an LLM judge to check JSON validity,
pytest exit codes, or SQL syntax — run a 0-token code assertion first.
Who Validates the Validators: Human criteria evolve as engineers
inspect real failures; re-align your binary rubric on 50 fresh traces
Cross-Family Calibration: Grade with a different model family than the
generator and report TPR, TNR, and Cohen's κ on every eval run.
If you cannot show the confusion matrix (TPR, TNR, κ), you do not have an eval judge — you have an opinion generator.
Curated by Nitin Aggarwal • Google Cloud ADK + OpenHands Factory • Proprietary + Confidential
